#!/bin/sh
# Installer for thunderbird-mcp (https://github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp).
#
#   curl -fsSL https://mudler.github.io/thunderbird-mcp/install.sh | sh
#
# Fallback URL (same script, served from the repo):
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp/master/docs/install.sh | sh
#
# Environment:
#   VERSION  release tag to install (e.g. v0.1.0); defaults to the latest release
#   BINDIR   install directory; defaults to ~/.local/bin
set -eu

REPO="mudler/thunderbird-mcp"
BIN="thunderbird-mcp"
BINDIR="${BINDIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

err() { printf 'install: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
info() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }

case "$(uname -s)" in
  Linux) os=linux ;;
  Darwin) os=darwin ;;
  *) err "unsupported OS '$(uname -s)'. Windows and other platforms: download an archive from https://github.com/$REPO/releases" ;;
esac

case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64 | amd64) arch=amd64 ;;
  aarch64 | arm64) arch=arm64 ;;
  *) err "unsupported architecture '$(uname -m)' (need x86_64 or arm64)" ;;
esac

if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fetch() { curl -fsSL -o "$2" "$1"; }
elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  fetch() { wget -qO "$2" "$1"; }
else
  err "need curl or wget"
fi

tag="${VERSION:-}"
if [ -z "$tag" ]; then
  api="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest"
  tmpjson=$(mktemp)
  fetch "$api" "$tmpjson" || { rm -f "$tmpjson"; err "cannot reach $api"; }
  tag=$(grep -m1 '"tag_name":' "$tmpjson" | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
  rm -f "$tmpjson"
  [ -n "$tag" ] || err "could not determine the latest release tag; set VERSION=vX.Y.Z and retry"
fi

# GoReleaser asset names drop the leading "v" of the tag.
version=${tag#v}
archive="${BIN}_${version}_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
base="https://github.com/$REPO/releases/download/$tag"

workdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$workdir"' EXIT INT TERM

info "Downloading $BIN $tag ($os/$arch)..."
fetch "$base/$archive" "$workdir/$archive" || err "download failed: $base/$archive"
fetch "$base/checksums.txt" "$workdir/checksums.txt" || err "download failed: $base/checksums.txt"

want=$(grep " $archive\$" "$workdir/checksums.txt" | cut -d' ' -f1)
[ -n "$want" ] || err "$archive not found in checksums.txt"
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  got=$(sha256sum "$workdir/$archive" | cut -d' ' -f1)
else
  got=$(shasum -a 256 "$workdir/$archive" | cut -d' ' -f1)
fi
[ "$got" = "$want" ] || err "checksum mismatch for $archive (expected $want, got $got)"

tar -xzf "$workdir/$archive" -C "$workdir" "$BIN"

mkdir -p "$BINDIR" 2>/dev/null || true
if [ -d "$BINDIR" ] && [ -w "$BINDIR" ]; then
  install -m 0755 "$workdir/$BIN" "$BINDIR/$BIN"
else
  info "$BINDIR is not writable; using sudo."
  sudo mkdir -p "$BINDIR"
  sudo install -m 0755 "$workdir/$BIN" "$BINDIR/$BIN"
fi

info "Installed $BIN $tag to $BINDIR/$BIN"

case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$BINDIR:"*) ;;
  *) info "NOTE: $BINDIR is not on your PATH. Add it, e.g.: export PATH=\"$BINDIR:\$PATH\"" ;;
esac

info ""
info "Quick start (profile is auto-discovered; override with THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE):"
info "  THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE=~/.thunderbird/xxxx.default-release $BIN"

# Security model

## Read-only guarantees

- The server **never writes** to any Thunderbird-owned file: mbox/maildir, the
  gloda index, `abook.sqlite`, the calendar database, `key4.db`, or `logins.json`.
- Every SQLite database is opened read-only (`mode=ro`, and `immutable=1` where a
  Thunderbird process might hold it).
- All message mutations go through **IMAP**, so Thunderbird picks up the change on
  its next sync rather than the server editing local state behind its back.

## Local folders are read-only

POP and "Local Folders" accounts store mail in on-disk mbox files. Writing to them
while Thunderbird is running risks corruption, so `set_flags`, `move_message`, and
`delete_message` reject local folders with a clear error. Reading them
(`search_messages`, `get_message`) is fully supported.

## Path-traversal protection

Message references are opaque `<folderURI>#<key>` strings. For local folders the
key is a byte offset and the folder URI maps to an on-disk file. The resolver
rejects any path segment that is `.`/`..`/empty or contains a separator, and
verifies the resolved path stays within the account's mail directory — so a
crafted `message_ref` cannot read arbitrary files.

## Sending is opt-in

The four compose actions are absent from the tool schema unless
`THUNDERBIRD_ALLOW_SEND=true`, and are rejected by a handler backstop even if a
client bypasses the schema. `THUNDERBIRD_READ_ONLY=true` removes all mutating and
sending actions at once.

## Credentials

Passwords are decrypted only in memory and are never logged or returned by any
tool. A master-password-protected profile cannot be decrypted; the server degrades
to read-only rather than exposing an error in place of a credential.

# One-liner install — design

Date: 2026-07-21
Status: approved

## Goal

Offer a copy-paste one-liner that installs the latest released `thunderbird-mcp`
binary on Linux and macOS:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://mudler.github.io/thunderbird-mcp/install.sh | sh
```

## Design

### `docs/install.sh`

A POSIX-sh installer. It lives in `docs/` so the existing mkdocs GitHub Pages
deploy serves it at `https://mudler.github.io/thunderbird-mcp/install.sh`
(mkdocs copies non-markdown files in the docs dir into the site verbatim — no
pipeline changes). The raw.githubusercontent URL works as a fallback.

Behavior:

- Detect platform: `uname -s` → `linux`/`darwin` (anything else, including
  Windows shells, errors with a pointer to the GitHub releases page);
  `uname -m` → `amd64`/`arm64`.
- Resolve the release tag: `VERSION=vX.Y.Z` env override, otherwise the
  `tag_name` of `releases/latest` from the GitHub API (parsed with grep/sed,
  no jq dependency).
- Download `thunderbird-mcp_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` (GoReleaser strips
  the leading `v` in asset names) plus `checksums.txt` into a `mktemp -d`
  directory that is removed on exit, using `curl` or `wget` (whichever
  exists).
- Verify the archive's sha256 against `checksums.txt` (`sha256sum` or
  `shasum -a 256`); mismatch is a hard failure, nothing is installed.
- Extract and install the binary to `$HOME/.local/bin` by default; `BINDIR`
  overrides (e.g. `BINDIR=/usr/local/bin`; the script uses sudo only if the
  target directory is not writable). Warn if the target dir is not on `PATH`.
- Finish by printing the installed tag, the install path, and a
  `THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE` quick-start hint. The script does not execute the
  installed binary (it is an MCP stdio server; running it would try to open a
  profile).
- `set -eu`; clear error messages for unsupported platform, missing
  downloader, failed API resolution, and checksum mismatch.

### Docs

- README "Quick start" gains the one-liner as the first option.
- `docs/index.md` gets the same one-liner in its quick-start section.

## Non-goals

- Windows support in the script (releases page has zips).
- Package managers (Homebrew, AUR, …).
- Self-update; re-running the script upgrades in place, which is enough.

## Testing

- `shellcheck docs/install.sh` clean.
- End-to-end run against the latest published release (v0.1.0): default
  install into a temp `BINDIR`, checksum verified, binary present and
  executable; also exercise `VERSION` override and checksum-mismatch failure
  path.

name: Docs

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths: ['docs/**', 'mkdocs.yml', '.github/workflows/docs.yml']
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: pip install mkdocs-material
      - run: mkdocs build --strict
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: site
      - id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  # Triggered by pushing a v* tag. GoReleaser creates the GitHub release itself,
  # so we intentionally do NOT also trigger on `release: published` (that would
  # run this workflow a second time and GoReleaser would fail on the existing release).

permissions:
  contents: write
  packages: write

jobs:
  docker:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Docker metadata
        id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@v5
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/mudler/thunderbird-mcp
          tags: |
            type=semver,pattern={{version}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}
            type=raw,value=latest
      - name: Build and push (multi-arch)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          build-args: |
            VERSION=${{ github.ref_name }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}

  binaries:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - name: GoReleaser
        uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v6
        with:
          version: '~> v2'
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# 🐦 thunderbird-mcp

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that exposes a local **Thunderbird** profile — mail, contacts, and calendar — to an LLM.

[![CI](https://github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp/actions/workflows/release.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![ghcr.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/ghcr.io-mudler%2Fthunderbird--mcp-blue?logo=docker)](https://github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp/pkgs/container/thunderbird-mcp)

It works with any MCP client and is designed to pair with [LocalAI](https://localai.io/docs/features/mcp).

---

## What it does

`thunderbird-mcp` reads Thunderbird's **own on-disk state** directly and uses **IMAP/SMTP** for anything live. There is no Thunderbird extension or add-on to install, and it works whether or not Thunderbird is running.

| Data source | File in the profile | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts, SMTP, calendars | `prefs.js` | read |
| Full-text search index | `global-messages-db.sqlite` (gloda) | read-only |
| Credentials | `key4.db` + `logins.json` (NSS) | read-only, decrypted in pure Go |
| Contacts | `abook.sqlite` | read-only |
| Calendar | `calendar-data/local.sqlite`, `calendar-data/cache.sqlite` | read-only |
| Live mail | IMAP / SMTP | fetch, mutate, send |

It is a single, static, **CGO-free** Go binary.

**Expected latency while Thunderbird holds a lock.** SQLite databases are normally read live, even with Thunderbird running. When Thunderbird does hold an exclusive lock, the first affected request waits about 5 seconds for it, then falls back to copying the database to a private snapshot, so a large search index is not instant. Subsequent requests are served from that snapshot and are fast for the next 60 seconds. Startup can pay the same wait once per data source. This is expected behaviour, not a hang.

## Tools

Three domain tools, each driven by an `action` enum:

### `thunderbird_mail`
`list_accounts`, `list_folders`, `search_messages`, `get_message`, `list_recent`, `get_attachment`, `set_flags`, `move_message`, `delete_message`, `send_mail`, `reply_message`, `forward_message`, `save_draft`

### `thunderbird_contacts`
`search_contacts`, `get_contact`

### `thunderbird_calendar`
`list_calendars`, `list_events`

The `action` enum is built **dynamically**: write actions (`set_flags`/`move_message`/`delete_message`) appear only when writes are allowed, and send actions (`send_mail`/`reply_message`/`forward_message`/`save_draft`) only when `THUNDERBIRD_ALLOW_SEND=true`. A disabled action is not even present in the schema.

See [calendar range and recurrence semantics](docs/calendar.md) for calendar limits and timezone policy.

See [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md) for the full per-action parameter reference.

## Safety model

- **Never writes to any Thunderbird-owned file** (mbox/maildir/gloda/abook/calendar/`key4.db`/`logins.json`). Every SQLite database is opened read-only. All mutations go through IMAP, where the server syncs.
- **Local (POP/Local Folders) accounts, contacts, and calendar are read-only.**
- **Sending is gated** behind `THUNDERBIRD_ALLOW_SEND=true` (off by default). `THUNDERBIRD_READ_ONLY=true` disables every mutating and sending action.
- Local message paths are resolved with **path-traversal protection** — a crafted `message_ref` cannot escape the profile directory.

More detail in [docs/security.md](docs/security.md).

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE` | auto-discovered | path to the profile directory |
| `THUNDERBIRD_READ_ONLY` | `false` | when `true`, mutating and sending actions are unavailable |
| `THUNDERBIRD_ALLOW_SEND` | `false` | when `true`, the compose/send actions are enabled |
| `THUNDERBIRD_TOOLS` | all | comma-separated allowlist of the three tool names |

## Quick start

### One-liner (Linux/macOS)

```bash
curl -fsSL https://mudler.github.io/thunderbird-mcp/install.sh | sh
```

Installs the latest release binary (amd64/arm64) to `~/.local/bin` after verifying its checksum against the release's `checksums.txt`. `BINDIR=/usr/local/bin` changes the destination, `VERSION=v0.1.0` pins a release.

### Docker

```bash
docker run -i --rm --network host \
  -e THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE=/profile \
  -v "$HOME/.thunderbird/xxxx.default-release:/profile:ro" \
  ghcr.io/mudler/thunderbird-mcp:latest
```

`--network host` lets the container reach your IMAP/SMTP servers; mounting the profile read-only is recommended (the server never writes to it).

### From source

```bash
go install github.com/mudler/thunderbird-mcp@latest
THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE=~/.thunderbird/xxxx.default-release thunderbird-mcp
```

### LocalAI

Add to your model configuration:

```yaml
mcp:
  stdio: |
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "thunderbird": {
          "command": "docker",
          "args": [
            "run", "-i", "--rm", "--network", "host",
            "-e", "THUNDERBIRD_PROFILE=/profile",
            "-e", "THUNDERBIRD_ALLOW_SEND=false",
            "-v", "/home/user/.thunderbird/xxxx.default-release:/profile:ro",
            "ghcr.io/mudler/thunderbird-mcp:latest"
          ]
        }
      }
    }
```

## Limitations (non-goals)

- **OAuth2** accounts are not supported for live IMAP/SMTP (most Gmail/Outlook setups). They still appear in index search; live fetch/send report a clear "unsupported" error.
- A profile protected by a **master password** cannot have its credentials decrypted — the server logs a warning and keeps the read-only search/contacts/calendar tools working.
- No calendar or contact **writes**.

## Development

```bash
go test ./...          # ginkgo suite
go vet ./...
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build .
```

The credential-decryption path is covered by a regression test against a **real** NSS `key4.db`/`logins.json` fixture (generated by the NSS library itself), in addition to synthetic round-trip tests.

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

# Bounded recurrence engine

This directory contains teambition/rrule-go v1.8.2, pinned to commit
`429348ca4477691b08edb0200b7f837edd32414c`.
Source: https://github.com/teambition/rrule-go/tree/429348ca4477691b08edb0200b7f837edd32414c
The upstream MIT license and regression tests accompany the source.

Local changes add `RRule.Work` and `RRule.Err`. The iterator calls `Work`
before every frequency period, including periods with no matches.
A callback error terminates iteration synchronously. No worker goroutine survives
cancellation. This hook is necessary because upstream `UNTIL` checks occur only
when a candidate matches; an impossible rule can search through year 9999.

The calendar adapter rejects subdaily frequencies, which contain additional
internal search loops. It limits time expansions to one time per day.
It calls each rule separately: upstream `Set` stores only one RRULE.

When updating this copy, preserve the callback and run the upstream tests plus
`TestCalendarExpansionBounds`. Do not replace it with an unguarded iterator.

package main

import (
	"database/sql"
	"os"

	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
	_ "modernc.org/sqlite"
)

func seedDB(seedFile string) string {
	tmp, _ := os.CreateTemp("", "seed-*.sqlite")
	tmp.Close()
	seed, err := os.ReadFile(seedFile)
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+tmp.Name())
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	_, err = db.Exec(string(seed))
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	db.Close()
	return tmp.Name()
}

var _ = Describe("Contacts.Search", func() {
	It("pivots properties into contacts and matches by name or email", func() {
		c, err := openContactsAt(seedDB("testdata/abook_seed.sql"))
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		defer c.Close()
		res, err := c.Search("bob", 10)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(res).To(HaveLen(1))
		Expect(res[0].Name).To(Equal("Bob Jones"))
		Expect(res[0].Email).To(Equal("bob@example.com"))
	})
})

import (

func buildGlodaFixture() *Gloda {
	tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "gloda-*.sqlite")
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	tmp.Close()
	seed, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/gloda_seed.sql")
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+tmp.Name())
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	_, err = db.Exec(string(seed))
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	db.Close()
	g, err := openGlodaAt(tmp.Name())
	Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
	return g
}

var _ = Describe("Gloda.Search", func() {
	var g *Gloda
	BeforeEach(func() { g = buildGlodaFixture() })
	AfterEach(func() { g.Close() })

	It("finds by body text and excludes deleted and ghost rows", func() {
		res, err := g.Search(SearchQuery{Text: "report", Limit: 10})
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(res).To(HaveLen(1))
		Expect(res[0].Subject).To(Equal("Quarterly report"))
		Expect(res[0].Ref).To(Equal("imap://alice@example.com/INBOX#101"))
		Expect(res[0].Date.Year()).To(Equal(2023))
	})
	It("filters by folder", func() {
		res, err := g.Search(SearchQuery{FolderURI: "imap://alice@example.com/Archive", Limit: 10})
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(res).To(HaveLen(1))
		Expect(res[0].Subject).To(Equal("Archive note"))
	})
	It("filters by from", func() {
		res, err := g.Search(SearchQuery{From: "carol", Limit: 10})
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(res).To(HaveLen(1))
		Expect(res[0].Author).To(Equal("carol@example.com"))
	})
	It("orders recent newest-first and never returns deleted/ghost", func() {
		res, err := g.Recent("", 10)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(res).To(HaveLen(3))
		Expect(res[0].Subject).To(Equal("Lunch")) // 1700100000000000 newest of the valid rows
	})
})

package main

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"

	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
)

var _ = Describe("ParseMessage", func() {
	It("extracts headers, text body and attachment metadata", func() {
		raw := "From: bob@example.com\r\n" +
			"To: alice@example.com\r\n" +
			"Subject: Report\r\n" +
			"Message-ID: <m1@example.com>\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8\r\n\r\n" +
			"the body\r\n"
		d, err := ParseMessage("imap://h/INBOX#1", []byte(raw))
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(d.Subject).To(Equal("Report"))
		Expect(d.Author).To(ContainSubstring("bob@example.com"))
		Expect(d.MessageID).To(Equal("<m1@example.com>"))
		Expect(d.BodyText).To(ContainSubstring("the body"))
	})
})

var _ = Describe("readMboxAt", func() {
	It("reads a single message at an offset", func() {
		dir := GinkgoT().TempDir()
		p := filepath.Join(dir, "INBOX")
		content := "From - Mon Jan 1\r\nSubject: one\r\n\r\nbody one\r\n" +
			"From - Mon Jan 2\r\nSubject: two\r\n\r\nbody two\r\n"
		Expect(os.WriteFile(p, []byte(content), 0o600)).To(Succeed())
		off := uint32(len("From - Mon Jan 1\r\nSubject: one\r\n\r\nbody one\r\n"))
		raw, err := readMboxAt(p, off)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(string(raw)).To(ContainSubstring("body two"))
		Expect(string(raw)).NotTo(ContainSubstring("body one"))
	})
})

var _ = Describe("ExtractAttachment", func() {
	It("extracts first attachment by index 0", func() {
		// Minimal multipart message with one attachment
		raw := "From: sender@example.com\r\n" +
			"To: recipient@example.com\r\n" +
			"Subject: Test\r\n" +
			"MIME-Version: 1.0\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=boundary123\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"--boundary123\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"body text\r\n" +
			"--boundary123\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n" +
			"Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"test.txt\"\r\n" +
			"Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"dGVzdCBjb250ZW50\r\n" +
			"--boundary123--\r\n"
		fn, ct, data, err := ExtractAttachment([]byte(raw), 0, 25*1024*1024)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(fn).To(Equal("test.txt"))
		Expect(ct).To(Equal("application/octet-stream"))
		Expect(data).NotTo(BeEmpty())
	})

	It("returns error on negative index", func() {
		raw := "From: test@example.com\r\nSubject: Test\r\n\r\nbody"
		_, _, _, err := ExtractAttachment([]byte(raw), -1, 25*1024*1024)
		Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(err.Error()).To(ContainSubstring("index must be >= 0"))
	})

	It("returns error on out-of-range index with count", func() {
		raw := "From: test@example.com\r\nSubject: Test\r\n\r\nbody"
		_, _, _, err := ExtractAttachment([]byte(raw), 5, 25*1024*1024)
		Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(err.Error()).To(ContainSubstring("attachment index 5 not found"))
		Expect(err.Error()).To(ContainSubstring("message has 0 attachments"))
	})

	It("uses fallback name when filename is empty", func() {
		raw := "From: sender@example.com\r\n" +
			"Subject: Test\r\n" +
			"MIME-Version: 1.0\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=b\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"--b\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: application/pdf\r\n" +
			"Content-Disposition: attachment\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"pdf data\r\n" +
			"--b--\r\n"
		fn, ct, data, err := ExtractAttachment([]byte(raw), 0, 25*1024*1024)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(fn).To(Equal("attachment-0"))
		Expect(ct).To(Equal("application/pdf"))
		Expect(data).NotTo(BeEmpty())
	})

	It("defaults to octet-stream when content-type is missing/empty", func() {
		// Note: MIME parsers typically default to text/plain when no Content-Type
		// is specified. Our fallback handles truly empty strings from parsing.
		raw := "From: sender@example.com\r\n" +
			"Subject: Test\r\n" +
			"MIME-Version: 1.0\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=b\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"--b\r\n" +
			"Content-Type:\r\n" +
			"Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"noct\"\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"binary data\r\n" +
			"--b--\r\n"
		fn, ct, data, err := ExtractAttachment([]byte(raw), 0, 25*1024*1024)
		Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(fn).To(Equal("noct"))
		// Even with empty Content-Type header, parser may assign default
		Expect(ct).NotTo(BeEmpty())
		Expect(data).NotTo(BeEmpty())
	})

	It("enforces size limit without loading entire file", func() {
		raw := "From: sender@example.com\r\n" +
			"Subject: Test\r\n" +
			"MIME-Version: 1.0\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=b\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"--b\r\n" +
			"Content-Type: text/plain\r\n" +
			"Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=\"big.txt\"\r\n" +
			"\r\n" +
			"this is huge data\r\n" +
			"--b--\r\n"
		_, _, _, err := ExtractAttachment([]byte(raw), 0, 5) // limit to 5 bytes
		Expect(err).To(HaveOccurred())
		Expect(err.Error()).To(ContainSubstring("exceeds size limit"))
	})
})

var _ = Describe("SanitizeFilename", func() {
	It("keeps simple filenames", func() {
		Expect(SanitizeFilename("document.pdf")).To(Equal("document.pdf"))
	})

	It("strips directory paths", func() {
		Expect(SanitizeFilename("../../../etc/passwd")).To(Equal("passwd"))
		Expect(SanitizeFilename("/path/to/file.txt")).To(Equal("file.txt"))
		Expect(SanitizeFilename("path\\to\\file.txt")).To(Equal("file.txt"))
		Expect(SanitizeFilename("C:\\Windows\\System32\\file.txt")).To(Equal("file.txt"))
	})

	It("returns basename for single dot", func() {
		Expect(SanitizeFilename(".")).To(Equal("."))
	})

	It("returns dot for empty filename", func() {
		// filepath.Base("") returns "." on all systems
		Expect(SanitizeFilename("")).To(Equal("."))
	})
})
